With two or more apps (several apps in one DSH; ARCHITECTURE.md §6): for the default app, the plugin-wide values are enough, but for a non-default app, unless you write its per-app fields, not even the default app's values are used (it runs empty). For each non-default app: - applications.<id>.webUrl of bridge-notify (the origin prepended to relative links in notifications; without it, that app's notification links are empty) and, if needed, bots - applications.<id>.webUrl of bridge-approvals (the URL of the approval screen, with {id} replaced by the approval ID) and, if needed, bots. The template's global webUrl (BRIDGE_WEB_PUBLIC_URL or http://127.0.0.1:3010 plus /approvals?id={id}) is not a <placeholder>, so check.mjs does not count it. Change the default app's value to your own approval screen as well - application: <id> in agents[] of bridge-assistant (an AI employee without it belongs to the default app, and the business web app's panel would point at another app) - linkGuard.webUrls.<id> of bridge-identity (9), and delegation for automatic tasks ("non-default apps" in b.7)

b.6 Business web app screens (web-kit) and the BFF

Screen Component Who
IM bot connection (Settings › IM bots) ImBotsShell mode="admin" (shows dsh-im's settings components with the --dbw-* CSS variables. channels is required: channelDefs(DEFAULT_CHANNELS, loaders). dsh-im's client components are loaded by the business web app's bundler through createImRuntime({ loadVendor, loadWeixin }) 〔web-kit README "Use it"〕. Use excludeBotIds to leave out staff members' personal bots) Administrators (organisation bots only)
Chat (SNS) linking (Settings › SNS linking) SnsLinkPage: ① own bots (ImBotsShell in self mode with personalChannels + personalRpc; all channels) ② link codes for organisation bots ③ own links and unlinking ④ notification settings All staff members (only their own links and their own bots)
Notification settings NotifyPrefsCard (types come from the server = the notification events in the manifest; descriptions come from the business side; hours in which notifications are held back). labels are events.<type>.label from the manifest (the manifest can only be fetched with the service token, so build them from the manifest when the business web app is built) All staff members
AI employee settings (Admin › AI employee settings) AiProfilePage (nickname, first-person pronoun, tone, company introduction, personality, background, speech examples, preview of the signature and sections, version list and 「この版に戻す」 (Restore this version); endpoint defaults to /bridge/v1/admin/ai-profile). By default, do not pass agents: there is one nickname (saving removes the per-AI-employee overrides of earlier versions). Only when each AI employee 〔preset〕 gets its own nickname, use agents={[{ id: <preset id>, name }]} (d.11) Administrators only
Attachment settings AttachmentSettingsCard (the roles and file types that may be attached; endpoint defaults to /bridge/v1/admin/assistant/attachment-settings; d.12) Administrators only
External connectors (Admin › External connectors) ExternalConnectorsPage (emergency stop, connections, templates, secrets 〔sent once; the list shows the last 4 characters〕, connection test, rules, run log; base defaults to /bridge/v1/admin; b.9) Administrators only
Help (manual) web-kit core's manualChapters / parseMarkdown (renders the same Markdown without injecting HTML; the target of manualUrl in AI answers, b.8) All staff members
Approval, AI proposal and AI assistant panels Not in the framework; build them per business. The AI proposal screen uses server-kit's routes: list GET /bridge/v1/proposals (?status=pending_review and so on; the person's own session), accept POST /bridge/v1/proposals/{proposalId}/accept, reject POST /bridge/v1/proposals/{proposalId}/reject ({ comment }). Only people in roles.proposalReviewers (by default, the readers of the report) can accept or reject, only once, and only on accept does the kit call proposalKinds[kind].apply in the same transaction. The approval screen uses the business system's own /api/* (mayDecide and decide, t.revokeApprovalDeliveries; b.2, b.3) —
tsx
<WebKitProvider runtime={runtime}
  meIm={createMeImClient({ base: '/bridge/v1', weixinBase: '/api/me/im/weixin' })}   // same origin, the person's own session
  adminRpc={createAdminRpc('/dsh/api/dsh-im')}                                         // the BFF's DSH gateway
  strings={{ 'sns.title': '外部アカウント連携' }}>
  <SnsLinkPage isAdmin={user.role === 'admin'} notify={{ role: user.role, labels: manifestEventLabels }} />
</WebKitProvider>

BFF rules (enforced by the BFF and the business system; web-kit only hides components the person cannot change):

  • Put @dsh-bridge/gateway before the /api/* proxy (gateway.handleRequest(req, res); for WebSocket, handleUpgrade). getSessionUser calls the business API's login check (e.g. GET /api/auth/me) with the req's cookie. isAllowed is normally admins only (the DSH settings screens /dsh/*).
  • Forward browser requests to the business system only for the routes that web-kit components call on the same origin and for the business /api/*: /bridge/v1/me/* (SnsLinkPage, NotifyPrefsCard), /bridge/v1/admin/ai-profile* (AiProfilePage), /bridge/v1/assistant/attachment-settings and /bridge/v1/admin/assistant/attachment-settings (attachments), /bridge/v1/admin/connector* (ExternalConnectorsPage), /bridge/v1/proposals and /bridge/v1/proposals/*/accept|reject (the AI proposal screen you build per business). Pass the person's cookie through as is, and do not add x-bff-secret (the business system authorises by the person's session and role).
  • MUST add x-bff-secret only to calls the BFF itself builds on the server side: the web assistant ticket (POST /bridge/v1/assistant/tickets), attachment conversion (POST /bridge/v1/assistant/attachments/prepare, callPrepare of prepareAssistantAttachments), and registering a personal bot right after a createOnly creation through the self-service RPC has succeeded (POST /bridge/v1/me/personal-bots, d.9). Do not forward these requests when they come from the browser (if they were relayed with the secret, a browser could register an organisation bot's botId as its own personal bot, and every other staff member who talks to that bot would become "unlinked").
  • AI assistant in the business web app: the BFF obtains a ticket, runs any attachments through prepareAssistantAttachments, and calls gateway.rpc('/assistant', 'message.send', { ticket, agent, text, attachments }, { plugin: 'bridge-assistant' }) (POST /api/bridge-assistant/assistant). Never expose the ticket, the DSH cookie or the launch token to the browser. The personal WeChat QR uses gateway.rpc('/weixin', 'provision.begin' | …) (begin | poll | verify | cancel under weixinBase of createMeImClient are routes the BFF builds; if you do not use them, set weixinBase: null). In both cases, only what you list in rpcAllowlist gets through.
  • If you offer personal bots, build a self-service RPC in the BFF (POST /api/me/im/rpc/<channel>). It is not a framework component, and there is no sample in the framework either (what to enforce is all of the MUSTs in d.9: a per-channel allowlist, botId only the person's own, narrowing the response's bots[] to the person's own, creating with createOnly: true, registering the new botId and deleting it on failure. CareBilling keeps it in apps/care-web/me-im-rpc.mjs). Before bot.delete, the BFF checks with the business API (GET /bridge/v1/me/personal-bots) that the bot belongs to the person.

b.7 Enable automatic tasks (delegate)

An automatic-task turn has no IM sender, so by default it cannot read business data (unattendedPolicy: deny). The operator chooses one staff member (linked via IM, with a role that can do the reads and proposals the task needs), and the tasks run under that staff member's delegation.

sh
node profile/scripts/install.mjs --home <home> --enable-auto-tasks --auto-task-delegate <platform>:<userId>[:<teamId>]
node profile/scripts/install.mjs --home <home> --disable-auto-tasks [ids]
node profile/scripts/install.mjs --home <home> --auto-task-delegate off          # back to deny
# manifest playbooks (after DSH has started once and plugin-events has deployed them): specify the ids
node profile/scripts/install.mjs --home <home> --skip-install --enable-auto-tasks pb_equipment-inspection_overdue_followup

To use different delegates for different kinds of work, write a class in the playbook's delegation (source.delegation in templates) and choose a staff member per class:

sh
node profile/scripts/install.mjs --home <home> --auto-task-delegate planning=line:<userId>,billing=line:<userId>,inspector=each[,default=line:<userId>]

  • <class>=<platform>:<userId>: playbooks of that class run under that staff member's delegation (unattendedDelegates of bridge-tools).

  • <class>=each: playbooks of that class (delegation: <class>=each) run on each run under the delegation of the person themself named by the triggering event. The business system answers POST /bridge/v1/delegations { event: { id } } by issuing a short-lived delegation to the person written in its own event (the business system decides which event types, how recent, and which personal settings qualify; in server-kit, hooks.eventDelegations (b.2). The DSH side cannot choose the staff member.

  • A class with no staff member assigned uses default (= the former unattendedOnBehalfOf). Templates with <class>=each are not enabled by --enable-auto-tasks (ids omitted), only when named by id. While a class is not each, install.mjs warns that "tools will be rejected".

  • Do not choose a broad role (such as administrator) as the delegate. If you list roles in unattendedWarnRoles of bridge-tools, a warning is logged once when a task runs under the delegation of such a role.

  • --auto-task-delegate writes unattendedPolicy: delegate and unattendedOnBehalfOf (unattendedDelegates when classes are used) into the product's own bridge-tools entry of the installed cordis.patch.yml (toolModules and the rest stay unchanged; if the entry is missing, it is appended at the end). It survives reinstalls, and off restores the original.

  • This value applies only to the default application (default: true in the registry, or the only app). For a non-default app, write by hand in the product patch's bridge-tools applications: { <application-id>: { unattendedPolicy: delegate, unattendedOnBehalfOf: …, unattendedDelegates: … } } (install.mjs does not write this field; sample in the template comments), or write it in the registry's applications[].delegation. Precedence: bridge-tools.applications.<id> → for the default app, the plugin-wide bridge-tools values → the registry. If you list several apps with strict: true and no default, --auto-task-delegate applies to no app, and automatic tasks silently stay without delegation (rejected) (unattendedPolicy in the plugins/tools README).

  • Hand-written delegation (unattendedPolicy: delegate in bridge-tools.applications.<id> or in the registry's delegation) is treated by check.mjs as an explicit opt-in (rule unattendedPolicy; writing it alone makes Definition of Done 6 fail). Run Definition of Done 6 with --allow unattendedPolicy, and leave the reason (which class is entrusted to a staff member with which narrow role) in a comment above that line of the patch. The value that --auto-task-delegate writes into the install target does not go into the product patch (source), so it does not need this treatment.

  • plugin-events deploys manifest playbooks as pb_<application-id>_<playbook> (new ones are disabled). --enable-auto-tasks <ids> / --disable-auto-tasks <ids> also work on deployed playbooks, but only when the ids are given explicitly.

  • A playbook's agent (e.g. facility-inspection) becomes a dedicated conversation preset. Define that preset in the product profile.

  • Only reads and the proposals listed in the task's source.tools (the playbook's tools) are allowed. Proposals and audit records are in that staff member's name. If bridge-tools is loaded, the read tools that bridge-apps generates from the manifest are also authorised through ctx.bridgeTools.gate(<appId>), so automatic-task delegation (and the subject of scheduled reports) applies in the same way to generated tools and hand-written tools.

  • Tasks owned by the deployment are profile/template/auto-tasks/*.json (format in profile/template/auto-tasks/README.md).

  • auto-tasks re-reads tasks.json on every event (enabling needs no restart). Changes to delegation (patch) and to plugin code need a DSH restart.

b.8 The manual and how-to questions over chat (help)

When a staff member asks over chat "Where is X?" or "How do I do X?", the AI secretary answers based only on the business system's manual, with the URL of a screen that person can open. Accuracy is kept by "the manual does not drift from the screens (CI)" and "the AI never makes up URLs (only paths from the index, checked before sending)".

  1. Manual: docs/manual/NN-*.md (the location is up to you; equipment-inspection uses manual/). One screen = one section (## Screen name, <a id="manual-…"></a>, a table: URL, menu, roles that can use it, related screens, keywords; body: what you can do, steps, cautions, FAQ). The format is in packages/help/README.md. Synonyms go in _synonyms.yml, and routes without a section go in _exclude.txt (write the reason).
  2. Index and CI: a script reads the manual and the business system's route table ([{ path, roles }], from the router and Guards), runs buildHelpIndex → commit the JSON. In CI, compare it with serializeIndex(buildHelpIndex(...)) and check that check* (routes, coverage, roles, menu names, anchors, links, notification links) is empty. The same script writes the manifest's web.routes (setManifestWebRoutes(text, routes): if the manifest has web:, it replaces the routes inside it; otherwise it adds web: before roles:). Keep the routes listed in _exclude.txt in the route table too (removing them from the table makes check* fail with "exclusion … is no route any more"). The sample equipment-inspection uses a simplified form: it has one screen (/), so the index is built at startup in src/help.mjs (neither committed nor compared with serializeIndex), and test/help.test.mjs only checks that check* is empty and checks the answers. The manifest's web.routes is written by hand with the same value as the screen table (/ only) (b.5 item 9). Systems with many screens commit and compare the index and write web.routes (CareBilling uses tools/manual-index.mjs).
  3. API: with server-kit, createBridgeApp({ help: createHelpService(index, { webBase, roleLabels, manualPage }) }). If you log questions with help.onQuestion, do not keep personal data (CareBilling keeps only text that passed the PII check, for 90 days).
  4. manifest: help: { tool: <ns>_help_search }, and that tool (GET /bridge/v1/help/search, read, all roles) in tools. DSH generates this tool as the manual search. Paste the text returned by helpRules('<ns>_help_search') (@dsh-bridge/dsh-core) into the AI employee persona (the prefix of the preset in the product profile) (YAML cannot call functions, so print it once with node and copy it; b.5).
  5. DSH: put the business web app URL (the same value as on the side that builds the answer URLs) in bridge-identity's linkGuard: webUrl for the default app, webUrls.<application-id> for the other apps. For an app with no URL, link checking does nothing (fail open. For an app that has web.routes but no URL, bridge-identity warns once, at that app's first AI answer), so write it for every app (link_guard in check.mjs verifies this). Checking works only when there is both a URL and web.routes (2) in the manifest. Answers from public sections to unlinked senders (publicHelp) are enabled when the manifest has help.
  6. Business web app: put the help screen at manualPage (default /help/{chapter}#{id}) (render the same Markdown with web-kit core's manualChapters). That route also goes into web.routes.

Rules: write answers only from the returned sections (if found=false, say that nothing was found and do not invent steps). Use the returned URLs as they are. For screens the person cannot open, do not give the URL; tell them to ask a role listed in alt. Answer questions about business data with the business tools.

b.9 External connectors (connections, operations, rules)

A mechanism for AI employees to use your company's other APIs and third-party APIs (accounting, attendance, maps, CRM and so on) (optional; the design and decisions are in docs/AI_EMPLOYEE_PROFILE.md §3 and "Implementation record (P2, P3)"). Both the secrets and the calls live in the business system: the AI and DSH do not know the connection URLs or API keys; they only call the business system's routes under delegation.

  1. server-kit: createBridgeApp({ connectors: { secretKey, allowLocalhost?, onApprovalNeeded?, onProposeByAi?, onRunResult? } }). secretKey is key material of 32 characters or more (API keys are sealed with AES-256-GCM and stored). Pass it from an environment variable; never write it in the repository or yml (equipment-inspection uses EQUIPMENT_CONNECTOR_KEY and rejects the default value in production). allowLocalhost is for development only. The tables are bridge_connector* (store.migrate()). Routes: GET /bridge/v1/connectors/catalog (service, etag; no URLs or secrets), POST /bridge/v1/connectors/{connectorId}/operations/{operationId}/run (delegation, read only; role ∈ operation.roles; a write gets 403 write_requires_approval), and for administrators (roles.admins) /bridge/v1/admin/connectors* (connections, secrets, connection test), /admin/connector-rules*, /admin/connector-runs and /admin/connector-settings (emergency stop). A proposal kind connector_write is added (do not use the same name in your own proposalKinds).
  2. Rules: add kit.connectors.tick() to a startScheduler task (every minute; b.3). A trigger is a manifest event or cron; conditions are only equals, contains, greater/less than and exists; mode is approval (default) / auto (only reads, and idempotent writes that an administrator has allowed with a written reason) / propose-by-ai. Events from before the feature was enabled are ignored.
  3. Write operations need human approval: AI tools do not execute writes; they create a connector_write proposal (the business system executes it on accept; on failure, 502 connector_failed, and the proposal stays pending). A rule's approval hands off to the business system's approval mechanism (approvals and recipient rules in b.2) through onApprovalNeeded({ proposal, connector, operation, rule, approverRole }, ctx). propose-by-ai starts a business-system automatic task through onProposeByAi (if absent, it is treated as approval). Results go to onRunResult (status and category only).
  4. DSH: with paths: v1, the routes connectorCatalog / connectorRun / connectorPropose stay at their defaults. bridge-tools builds <namespace>_ext_<connection>_<operation> from the catalog (read runs under the person's delegation, write becomes a proposal; connectorTools / connectorRefreshSeconds). Never write connection URLs or secrets in the DSH profile.
  5. Business web app: web-kit ExternalConnectorsPage for the admin-only "External connectors" screen. The BFF forwards /bridge/v1/admin/connector* with the person's cookie as is and without the secret (b.6).
  6. The rules are in d.13. Start with one or two reads.

b.10 External mode: put the bridge outside the existing system (trial)

Trial (added 2026-10-30): not yet validated on a real system (PoC). It will change based on the validation results. The release conditions (52 / 52, empty knownGaps, no skips) do not change. The rationale is in EXTERNAL_LAYER_FEASIBILITY.md (in Chinese).

In this form you do not touch the existing system's code; instead you put a bridge-only service (the external bridge) outside it, which calls the existing system's API and exposes Bridge v1. The external bridge is built on server-kit, and the bridge_* tables live in the external bridge's own DB. From DSH's point of view the external bridge is the business system, so the DSH, plugin and IM sides do not change.

flowchart LR
  D["DSH<br/>(unchanged)"] -- "Bridge v1" --> X["External bridge<br/>server-kit, bridge_* tables<br/>ingested change IDs"]
  X -- "API (as the person)" --> L["Existing system<br/>(code unchanged)"]
  L -- "webhook / CDC<br/>(after commit)" --> X
  L -. "Login (IdP)" .- X

Is it a fit? Decide by four capabilities of the existing system

Capability Items used (table at the top) If missing
Login can be verified from outside (an OIDC / SAML IdP, or an endpoint that returns "who this session is") 3 (chat linking), 8 (session) 3 cannot be met. No separate login may be built (the MUST in 3), so external mode cannot be used
The API can be called as the person (per-user OAuth tokens, token exchange 〔RFC 8693〕, a trusted delegated identity) 1 (reads), 6, 7 Per-record permissions would have to be copied into the external bridge. Limit reads to the scope determined by role alone, and do not use approvals or writes
Change notification (a webhook meeting the conditions below, or reading the DB transaction log) 5 Events that need accuracy, such as approvals, cannot be emitted. Only status notices by polling (item 4 of ingestion below)
Approval and write APIs 1 (the proposal's apply), 7 Accepting proposals and approving in chat are not possible
  • Type A (all four; most SaaS and recent web systems): external mode can meet every item in the table at the top.
  • Type B (has an API but it cannot be called as the person, or there is no change notification): up to status notices, scheduled reports and read questions. If 7 (approval) cannot be met, you do not reach 52 / 52 (A1–A4 are skipped), so for a release either add what is missing to the existing system or rebuild with b.0.
  • Type C (screens only: server rendering only, desktop clients, terminals): do not use external mode. Writing through screen automation (RPA) is fragile and cannot be audited. Add an API to the existing system, or build with b.0.

Items met differently in external mode (numbers of the table at the top; the other items stay as in b.1–b.9)

# How it is met in external mode
1 Read tools are external-bridge routes that internally call the existing system's read API as the person. Proposals live in the external bridge, and only when a person accepts does proposalKinds[kind].apply call the existing system's write API as the person who accepted
3 The external bridge serves the chat-linking screen (web-kit). Login is done as a relying party of the existing system's IdP via OIDC / SAML, or by verifying the existing system's session through the "who" endpoint. authenticate(req) returns the existing system's staff ID. MUST not create a separate password or a separate ID scheme
4 recipientsFor decides by fetching the person in charge, approvers and affiliation from the existing system's API. MUST not invent assignment rules in the external bridge when these cannot be fetched (they would drift from existing operations). Do not notify for that event
5 Trial rule: event ingestion below
6 employees.get / list come from the existing system's staff API (including active/inactive). MUST not cache employees.get (a deactivated staff member must lose all tokens immediately: D7, S5). MUST not call read APIs with an all-powerful service account and filter in the external bridge (the per-record permission check would live in two places, breaking "the same check as the web authorisation" in 4)
7 approvals.mayDecide / decide call the existing system's approval API as the person. MUST not copy approval rules into the external bridge. Once the existing system has decided, write approval.decided in an external-bridge transaction and invalidate the IM card with t.revokeApprovalDeliveries. For approvals decided on the existing system's screens, do the same through ingestion (below). Only for business that has no approval in the existing system may a minimal approval live in the external bridge (there are no rules to copy, so nothing is duplicated)
8 isSessionLive calls the existing system's session-check endpoint

Trial rule: event ingestion (a variant of item 5 in the table at the top)

Item 5 in the table at the top and the "same transaction" of b.3 exist because picking up differences afterwards leads to "notifying changes that were never committed and dropping changes that were committed". The external bridge is not inside the existing system's transaction, so it cannot meet them literally. In external mode only, the following sources are allowed, because they can ingest only committed changes, without dropping or duplicating any.

  1. The source is one of the following.

    • (a) Same transaction (b.3), when you can write inside the existing system. Not the main form of external mode.
    • (b) DB transaction log (CDC): PostgreSQL logical replication, MySQL binlog, SQL Server CDC and so on. Only committed changes flow, in commit order. Needs read permission on the existing system's DB (the existing system's code does not change).
    • (c) A webhook meeting all of the following: ① sent after commit　② each change has a unique, immutable ID (change ID)　③ resent until the receiver returns 2xx　④ the sender can be verified, e.g. by a signature　⑤ there is a way to fill gaps later (an API to re-fetch by change ID or by time).

  2. MUST ingestion writes "the record of the ingested change ID" and kit.emitEvent in one transaction of the external bridge. From the second time for the same change ID onwards, it does nothing (decided by a unique constraint). This makes the path from the existing system's commit to the Bridge event "no drops, no duplicates".

    js
    // the external bridge's own table (not bridge_*): create table legacy_change (source text, change_id text, primary key (source, change_id))
export async function ingest(kit, change) {        // change = only the change ID, IDs, date and status extracted from one webhook / CDC item
  return kit.tx(async (t) => {
    const { rowCount } = await t.db.query(
      'insert into legacy_change (source, change_id) values ($1, $2) on conflict do nothing', ['billing', change.id])
    if (rowCount === 0) return { duplicate: true }    // second time onwards: do nothing
    await kit.emitEvent(t, {
      type: 'invoice.submitted', aggregateType: 'invoice', aggregateId: change.invoiceId,
      payload: { invoiceId: change.invoiceId, submittedOn: change.date },   // allowlisted keys only
    })
    return { duplicate: false }
  })
}
    • Needs the PostgreSQL store (createPostgresStore) (t.db is the connection of that transaction; in the memory store, t.db is null).
    • For a webhook, return 2xx only after ingestion has committed (returning first drops the change if ingestion fails).
    • If the manifest rejects the event (EventRejected), no change-ID record remains either, and the resends keep coming. This is a configuration error, so monitor the failure count so that you notice it.

  3. MUST build only the manifest's allowlisted keys from the existing system's values and pass them to emitEvent (no names, free text or health data; d.2).

  4. MUST use polling (periodically reading differences by updated_at and the like) only for status notices that do not need accuracy (e.g. "there are N unprocessed items"). It drops intermediate states and deletions, so do not use it for events where a drop hurts, such as approvals (approval.requested / approval.decided), deadlines and changes of amounts. Write in the external bridge's README which types are emitted by polling.

  5. SHOULD measure the delay from the existing system's commit to the Bridge event, set an upper limit (e.g. 1 minute) and monitor it. For CDC position lag and webhook failures, output counts only (not contents).

  6. SHOULD keep in mind that webhooks often do not guarantee order. If an older change for the same aggregate (aggregateId) arrives later, re-read the existing system's current state before emitting (not needed for CDC, which is in commit order).

conformance (b.4)

  • Use the 52 items as they are. BRIDGE_BASE_URL is the external bridge. The release conditions are the same.
  • The fixtures create business activity in the existing system's TEST environment and return after waiting until ingestion has finished (produceEvents, emitNotifiableEvent, createPendingApproval). newEmployee, deactivateEmployee and revokeSession are done on the existing system's side.
  • The 52 items do not check ingestion's "no drops, no duplicates". At a minimum, check it in the external bridge's tests: the same change sent twice gives one event / ingestion stopped before commit gives one event after the resend / 2xx comes after commit / the types emitted by polling include no approval, deadline or amount events.

Afterwards: migrate the business one piece at a time (Strangler Fig)

Run the AI employee first in external mode, then move the business one piece at a time to a new system per b.0 (on server-kit). For each migrated piece, switch the internals of the hooks from the existing system's API to the new tables, and bring the events back into the same transaction as in b.3. Bridge v1 is the seam, so the DSH side stays unchanged at every stage, and the 52 items can be re-run each time.

Cautions during the trial

  • server-kit has no external-mode-specific components yet (a client for the existing system's API, an ingestion component, an OIDC / SAML authenticate). As in the example above, you can write them today with kit.tx, kit.emitEvent and hooks. Keep safeguards for calling the existing system's API (allowed hosts only, timeouts, rate limits) along the same lines as createConnectorRunner (b.9). Whether to turn these into components will be decided after the PoC.
  • In external communication, you may say only as much as "if the existing system has SSO, an API and change notification, it can be connected without changing the existing system's code". Do not say "any system can be connected without changes" (types B and C cannot).

  • [ ] bridge-validate manifest --strict exits 0 (no warnings)
  • [ ] Every state change uses kit.tx + emitEvent (payload allowlist only). In external mode (trial), the sources and ingestion of b.10 (change ID and event in one transaction, polling only for status notices)
  • [ ] For a new system: the location and dependencies follow one of the options in b.0, and nothing inside the framework (packages, plugins, vendor, profile/template) has been rewritten
  • [ ] The manifest declares approval.requested / approval.decided / sns_identity.unlinked with the payloads of b.1
  • [ ] conformance 52 / 52, empty knownGaps, no skips (reports, approvals, personal bots, both proposal kinds and the fixtures' copy of the roles are all in place; b.4)
  • [ ] Registry: system.id = app id, tools are <namespace>_*, all bots listed (strict: true), tokens only as environment variable names
  • [ ] Message wording: intent on every template, action for action / urgent
  • [ ] DSH-side code (toolModules, templateModules, custom plugins) does not touch the business DB or the business system's secrets, and uses only kit.requestJson / kit.proposeTool (d.1)
  • [ ] Business web app: screens for chat linking, notification settings, approvals and proposals (proposals use GET /bridge/v1/proposals, …/{id}/accept, …/{id}/reject; b.6). The BFF adds x-bff-secret only to its own calls (ticket, attachment conversion, personal-bot registration after createOnly) and does not relay browser requests with the secret (b.6)

  • [ ] Recipients: for every notifiable event, recipientsFor decides the scope and the gate checks it. If the scope cannot be decided, nothing is sent (d.8)
  • [ ] Outbound settings: the template's closed values ("product values" in d.8) are kept (no fixed delivery targets, mail, model-chosen recipients or copies of launch replies). Every opened setting is an explicit opt-in with its reason written down
  • [ ] No names, free text, health data or Japanese sentences in payloads or template arguments (d.2)
  • [ ] If personal bots are used: self-service RPC, createOnly, excluded from the admin list. The owner rules for lookups are in server-kit (mandatory for your own implementation; d.9)

  • [ ] With two or more apps: for each non-default app, applications.<id>.webUrl (and bots) of bridge-notify / bridge-approvals, agents[].application of bridge-assistant, linkGuard.webUrls.<id>, and automatic-task delegation (b.5 item 10)
  • [ ] If how-to questions are answered over chat: manual CI (index up to date, check* empty), help.tool and web.routes in the manifest, the helpRules text in the persona (b.8)

Systems that hold names implement the roster check hooks.piiScan. Organisation memory classes and retention periods decided. The AI employee presets can use the memory_* tools (d.10)
  • [ ] AI employee profile (bridge-persona, included by default in the template): GET /bridge/v1/ai-profile and the admin routes exist (server-kit has them by default; your own implementation validates, versions and audits with validateAiProfile). The business web app has an admin-only "AI employee settings" screen (web-kit AiProfilePage, one nickname by default) (d.11)
  • [ ] File attachments to the AI assistant (optional): /bridge/v1/assistant/attachments/prepare, attachment-settings and the admin routes exist (server-kit has them by default; your own implementation checks and converts with @dsh-bridge/server-kit/extract), the handling of scanned PDFs decided (attachments.ocr: OCR engine / images to the default model / false), the BFF uses prepareAssistantAttachments, the panel has AssistantAttachmentPicker and a one-line note on where files are sent, answers use AssistantMarkdown, administrators get AttachmentSettingsCard (d.12)

Definition of Done (verified by commands)

The checklist items that can be verified by commands. Each is either a command the framework has today or a test the business system writes itself. The framework's e2e, which checks the DSH side end to end with a real DSH (pnpm run e2e, a.3), is currently specific to equipment-inspection (the app id is hard-coded in packages/testing/e2e/run.mjs), so the completion of a new system or a connected system is judged by conformance (2) and the business system's own tests (3–6).

# What Command Pass
1 manifest node <framework>/packages/protocol/bin/bridge-validate.mjs manifest bridge.manifest.yaml --strict exit 0 (with --strict, warnings also give exit 1. Without it, warnings still give exit 0, so it does not count as passing)
2 conformance Start the TEST environment, then BRIDGE_BASE_URL=… BRIDGE_SERVICE_TOKEN=… BRIDGE_BFF_SECRET=… BRIDGE_FIXTURES=./test/fixtures.mjs BRIDGE_MANIFEST_FILE=./bridge.manifest.yaml node --test <framework>/packages/protocol/conformance/http.test.mjs (the same as bridge-validate conformance). In CI, follow the form of equipment-inspection's test/conformance.test.mjs (startup, temporary DB and cleanup in one test) The summary is 52 passed, 0 known gaps, 0 skipped
3 The business system's own tests node --test test/*.test.mjs (on Windows, --test-isolation=none) All pass. At a minimum: state change and event in the same transaction (if the manifest rejects the payload, the business row does not remain either), the recipientsFor gate (staff outside the scope are not included; stale when the situation changes), web approval uses mayDecide and is decided exactly once, business writes with a delegation token get 403 delegation_not_permitted, the BFF does not relay the browser's POST /bridge/v1/me/personal-bots with the secret, hooks.piiScan returns a category for names on the roster
4 Manual (if used) In the business system's tests, checkAnchors, checkSectionPaths, checkCoverage, checkRoleText and checkLinks are empty; if the index is committed, serializeIndex(buildHelpIndex(...)) equals the committed index (the sample examples/equipment-inspection/test/help.test.mjs checks only check*; it is the simplified form that builds the index at startup; b.8) Empty, equal
5 Product profile node <framework>/profile/scripts/install.mjs --source <product profile> --home <temporary directory> --profile <name> --skip-install (a personal ~/.dsh is rejected) No template placeholders left warning
6 Outbound settings are closed node <framework>/profile/scripts/check.mjs <your profile>/cordis.patch.yml (closed values, opened values, bundled coding presets disabled, leftover <placeholder>; every app in the registry has a linkGuard URL 〔rule link_guard〕. Use --allow <rule> only for intended opt-ins; hand-written automatic-task delegation needs --allow unattendedPolicy, b.7). The other half of link checking (the manifest's web.routes) is written on the manifest side in 1 exit 0
7 Fixed delivery targets are rejected Add --auto-task-target x to the command in 5 exit 2

Checks with a real IM and real models are manual (e, g).

Example tool module (business data is read only with kit.requestJson, and writes are only kit.proposeTool proposals. It does not touch the business DB or secrets. d.1):

js
// my-app-tools.js
export const application = 'my-app'
export default (kit) => [
  kit.defineTool({ name: 'myapp_count_open', description: 'Read-only: open items count.', async execute() {
    return { ok: true, data: await kit.requestJson('myapp_count_open', '/api/open-items') } } }),
  kit.proposeTool({ name: 'myapp_propose_close', kind: 'close_item', description: 'propose closing one item.',
    parameters: { type: 'object', properties: { itemId: { type: 'string' } }, required: ['itemId'] },
    forbidden: ['amount'], forbiddenReason: 'amounts are computed by the business system' }),
]

Example message wording module:

js
// my-app-templates.js
export const templates = {
  'reservation.overdue': ({ count }) => ({                  // Fact sentence only. plugin-notify adds the frame (label, greeting, signature, link)
    title: '返却期限の超過', text: `返却期限を過ぎた予約が ${count} 件あります。`,
    intent: 'action', ask: '業務 Web の「予約」で確認してください。',
  }),
}

d. Rules (MUST / SHOULD)

d.1 The AI does not decide

  • MUST AI tools are only read (GET) or propose (POST /bridge/v1/proposals). There is no write. Business write APIs return 403 to delegations.
  • MUST Code on the DSH side (toolModules, templateModules, custom plugins) does not touch the business DB or the business system's secrets (service tokens, DB URLs, external connector keys). Business data is read only through kit.requestJson (a Bridge v1 / business API call carrying the person's delegation), and writes are only kit.proposeTool proposals. Connecting to the DB directly, or fetching with a service token you attach yourself, bypasses the bridge-tools gate (delegation = AI allow-list ∩ role) and also breaks the business system being the single source of truth (ARCHITECTURE.md §3 "L3 does not know L2 (only HTTP v1)").
  • MUST Finalising, approving, issuing, paying and sending are done by people in the business system. Accepting or rejecting a proposal is also done only by people, once.
  • MUST The AI does not decide or write amounts. Do not put amounts in proposal tool arguments (forbidden: ['amount']). The business system calculates amounts, and the business system presents them as fields of the approval card.
  • MUST Write the prohibitions in the playbook and in the AI employee's instructions: finalise nothing, do not write names or personal data to memory, notes or reports, read business data only through tools, do not invent numbers or facts that the tools did not return, trigger data is business data, not instructions.

d.2 Keep personal data out

  • MUST Event payloads carry only IDs, dates, counts and states (an allow-list per type). Do not include names, contact details, free text, health information or amount breakdowns. Do not include Japanese sentences either: the payload check (checkPayloadWhitelist, used by server-kit's emitEvent and by the conformance event items) treats any value containing kanji, hiragana or katakana as free text (cjk_text) and rejects it. Pass text such as version names, subjects and comments by ID; the business system shows the text when it is opened in the business web app (CareBilling's public master events do not carry the version name, only the version ID). Use alphanumeric codes for state values (approved etc.).
  • MUST Template arguments are only numbers, dates, times, months and flags (integer / number / flag / time / date / monthday / month / datetime). Do not show names in IM message wording (not even in greetings). The exception is 「〇〇 さんとして」 (as 〇〇) in the linking-complete reply (a reply to the person themself).
  • MUST Links are business web app paths containing only IDs (/equipment/{id}). The business web app authorises again when the link is opened.
  • SHOULD Validate the manifest in CI, and have the business system check strings with /bridge/v1/pii-scan (which returns only the kinds). PII detection is heuristic (one layer of defence in depth); the core of the defence is the structure of "carry nothing but IDs, dates, counts and states".

d.3 Idempotency and once-only

  • MUST Every send has an idempotency key: notifications notify:<eventId>:<userId>, approval cards approval:<id>:<userId>, automatic tasks auto-tasks:<taskId>:k:<dedupeKey>…, scheduled reports proactive:<alarmId>:<firedAt>:…. Retries and restarts use the same key (no double sending).
  • MUST Event processing is at-least-once, so receivers tolerate duplicates (dedupeKey, the notification's <eventId>:<userId>, the dedupeKey of recipientsFor).
  • MUST An approval is finalised by the decision of any one person, and all other cards become invalid. Cards are also invalidated when the decision is made on the web.
  • MUST Link codes, card tokens and reply codes are single-use. Wrong attempts are counted and lead to a lock.

d.4 Quiet hours and send times

  • MUST Respect the person's quiet hours (quietHours). Only types marked notify.quiet: exempt in the manifest (such as safety checks) may be delivered at night. honorQuietHours: false is for verification only.
  • SHOULD Send frequent types as digests (digestMinutes / digestTypes): one message saying 「N 件まとめてお知らせします。」 (Here are N items together.).

d.5 AI secretary message wording

Shape (4–6 lines on a smartphone, no emoji; "▶" and the "—" of the signature are symbols):

text
【ラベル】件名                        ← line 1: [label] subject (on a card: the subject)
<あいさつ><事実の文>                  ← <greeting><fact sentence>: counts, months, dates only. In a digest: 「N 件まとめてお知らせします。」
▶ お願いしたいこと（目安）：…         ← action request / urgent (what, where)
ご対応は不要です。…                   ← report
こちらから開けます：<URL>             ← when there is a link (a button on a card)
— <アプリ名> AI 秘書                  ← signature: — <app name> AI secretary (without an app name: 「— AI 秘書」)
Label intent When to use
【ご報告】 (Report) info Information only. Closes with 「ご対応は不要です。…」 (No action is needed. …)
【対応のお願い】 (Action requested) action Someone's judgement or operation is needed. 「▶ お願いしたいこと：何を・どこで（画面名）」 (▶ What we ask: what, where (screen name)); a target date only if it is in params
【至急】 (Urgent) urgent Safety checks, visits not started, serious incidents, etc.
【承認のお願い】 (Approval requested) (approval card) / approval The plugin-approvals approval card. A deadline only when expiresAt exists. A text notification without buttons (e.g. handing over to another person because the only possible approver is the person themself; the decision is made in the business web app) uses approval
【ご相談】 (Consultation) consult Matters where you want help thinking through a decision (notices of actions still unresolved past their deadline, checking decision material, etc.). Closes with the same 「▶ お願いしたいこと」 as action
【定時のご報告】 (Scheduled report) (scheduled report) Split into 「■ 対応が必要なこと」 (■ Needs action) and 「■ ご参考」 (■ For reference)
【ご案内】 (Guidance) (AI answer) / info Answers to how-to questions about the system (where a screen is, steps). The only basis is the business system's manual search tool, and links go only to screens the tool returned (bridge-identity's link check drops anything not in web.routes)
  • The greeting depends on the send time (system timezone): 5:00–9:59 「おはようございます。」 (Good morning.), 10:00–20:59 「お疲れさまです。」 (Thank you for your work.), 21:00–4:59 「夜分に失礼します。」 (Sorry to disturb you so late.).
  • Do not invent dates: target dates and deadlines only when they are in params. 「本日中」 (by the end of today) only for undated actions where it is clear in business terms.
  • On a shared bot (personal WeChat), 【アプリ名】 (app name) is prefixed (【設備点検】【対応のお願い】…).
  • Use frameMessage / frameAiText / noticeCard from @dsh-bridge/dsh-core for the frame; do not assemble it yourself.

お疲れさまです。3 件まとめてお知らせします。
本日の点検が 3 件完了しました。

こちらから開けます：https://inspection.example.jp/inspections

【承認のお願い】修理依頼

Link check: put web.routes (path patterns of the business web app's screens) in the manifest and set bridge-identity's linkGuard.webUrl to the business web app URL; business web app links in AI answers (IM turns) then point only to screens that exist (other hosts: linkGuard.allowHosts). A link whose URL the AI got wrong by even one character is not delivered.

Automatic task reports (the summary the AI writes) start with 「【対応のお願い】」 (needsDecision) or 「【ご報告】」; with 【対応のお願い】 the next line is 「▶ お願いしたいこと：誰が（役割名）・どこで・何を」 (▶ What we ask: who (role name), where, what). IDs as the first 8 characters; counts and dates only.

d.6 Platform notes

Platform Notes
Personal WeChat (iLink) One bot per account (shared with multiApp, switched with #一覧). Proactive sends use the conversation context last received from the user, and iLink accepts them only for a certain time after the user's last message (generally said to be 24 hours, but unverified). After that, weixin_context_missing makes the send undeliverable at once. Ask users to link another platform as well for important notifications
Microsoft Teams Proactive sends work only if the user has first talked 1:1 with the bot and a conversation reference exists (otherwise invalid_target). Ask users to send one message when linking
LINE Monthly send limit (HTTP 429 monthly limit → line_quota). It does not recover until the month changes or the plan is upgraded, so retry later and reduce the number of messages with digests. updateCard becomes a new send
email Notifications only. The sender cannot be verified, so linking, approval and AI use are not possible. Not in the default delivery priority (to use it, list it explicitly in platformPriority)
Lark (Feishu) The open_id is different for each app (bot). The same person links each app separately, and notifications are sent from the app that person linked
Slack An existing App needs a manifest update and reinstall for interactivity and im:write. The modal for entering a send-back reason (openReasonDialog) is Slack-only
WeCom Use self-built apps (wecom-app) to give each app its own contact point. The callback is /wecom-app-callback/<botId>/<secret> (the gateway's publicPrefixes)

d.7 Secrets and environment

  • MUST Do not write tokens or secrets in yml, the repository or logs. The registry holds only the names of environment variables (apiUrlEnv / serviceTokenEnv). The only exception is development defaults (fixed values that are not real secrets; startup is refused in production [NODE_ENV=production]. equipment-inspection's src/config.mjs. b.0).
  • MUST Run DSH in an isolated home (do not use a personal ~/.dsh). Do not expose the launch token to the browser.
  • MUST Tests use only fictitious data and test values, loopback only, and never the demo environment or production ports and DBs.

d.8 Recipient guarantees and outbound settings

Principle: each role and each account receives over SNS only the business notices, messages and requests that concern them. The business system decides who receives what; neither the AI nor the DSH settings decide it (ARCHITECTURE.md §7).

  • MUST The business system decides the recipients (recipientsFor / for-event). Send to everyone in a role only when the event really concerns the whole organisation (billing close, payroll, scheduled reports, etc.). Otherwise narrow it to the scope of the target (service user, office, person in charge), and at the gate check "whether that person can see the same target in the business web app" (b.2). If the scope is unknown, do not send.
  • MUST Do not let the AI choose destinations. Leave no model-callable tool that can specify a destination (bot, conversation, email address) (modelTools: reclaim, mail: false). Automatic task reports go only to the event's recipients; if no recipient is determined, nothing is sent (audienceFallback: none, restrictDelivery: true). install.mjs rejects fixed operator delivery targets (--auto-task-session / --auto-task-bot / --auto-task-target).
  • MUST Do not handle business in group conversations (groupChat: deny, the default). Even when the answer uses the speaker's own permissions, it is visible to the other people in the group. Use allow only when the business system side can say that everyone may see the same scope.
  • MUST For delegation in turns with no sender (automatic tasks), choose a narrow staff member for each kind of work (<class>) or use the person in the triggering event (<class>=each). Do not make an administrator the delegate for all tasks (detect it by listing broad roles in unattendedWarnRoles; the template does not list them, so the deployment does).
  • MUST Do not send AI free text to anyone other than the person themself. Automatic task reports use fixed message wording (audienceText: template). Scheduled reports go only to the person's 1:1 (deliveryGuard: required), and the body is aiReportGuard: screen (on a hit, the whole text becomes the fixed wording) or template.
  • SHOULD Do not rely too much on screenOutboundText. It works from word lists and pattern guesses, so names written only in hiragana, specific disease names and paraphrases get through. The core of the defence is the structure of "the AI reads only counts, and sends only to the person's 1:1". If business terms are wrongly matched as health terms, replace the list with healthWords (not yet in the plugin settings; pass it from the side that calls dsh-core directly).

List of settings (some plugin and fork "defaults" behave the same as upstream. The framework's profile template ships the closable outbound settings [from groupChat to forwardPluginSources in the table] written with the "product value", so a profile made from the template is closed in that respect. They can be opened only by an explicit change in the product patch (b.5). The bottom 4 rows of the table [from unattendedPolicy on] are per-deployment values, so the template does not include them: unattendedWarnRoles and linkGuard are written by the deployment [without them there is no detection or check]. unlinkedPolicy can stay at the default):

Setting Where Default Product value What happens if it is not closed
groupChat bridge-identity, bridge-tools, registry applications[].groupChat deny deny In group conversations, answers given under the speaker's permissions are visible to everyone
audienceFallback bridge-notify (all apps; overridden per applications.<id>) channels none Reports with no determined recipient go to the fixed delivery targets of auto-tasks
audienceText / audienceLink bridge-notify (all apps; overridden per applications.<id>) / applications.<id> summary / / template / a business web app screen AI text written under the delegated staff member's permissions reaches other recipients
aiReportGuard / aiReportLink bridge-notify (overridden per applications.<id>) screen / / screen or template With off, the scheduled report body is not checked
proactiveDelivery bridge-notify allow deny Business alarms other than scheduled reports are sent to IM
modelTools dsh-proactive (fork #13) all reclaim The AI in any conversation can send to any destination with deliver_to and can change alarms in other people's conversations
deliveryGuard dsh-proactive (fork #14) optional required When bridge-notify's outbound guard is absent, answers to business triggers are sent as they are
restrictDelivery dsh-auto-tasks (fork #16) false true Fixed delivery targets, test sends and auto_task_report from other conversations can be used
mail dsh-auto-tasks (fork #16) true false auto_task_mail (SMTP to any address) and mail polling and digests can be used
forwardPluginSources dsh-im (xmanrui-dsh-im) [] [] Trigger answers are copied to the conversation's IM without any check
unattendedPolicy / unattendedDelegates bridge-tools, registry applications[].delegation deny / none A narrow staff member per class, each (for the default app, install.mjs --auto-task-delegate writes it to the installation; unattendedPolicy: delegate written by hand in a product patch is opt-in: check.mjs needs --allow unattendedPolicy, with the reason in a comment. b.7) All automatic tasks run under the delegation of one person (a broad role)
unattendedWarnRoles bridge-tools [] [admin] etc. Delegation to broad roles goes unnoticed
unlinkedPolicy bridge-tools deny deny With ai-readonly, even unlinked senders get reads under the AI's own permissions
linkGuard.webUrl / webUrls.<id> bridge-identity none The business web app URL of every app (the default app in webUrl, others in webUrls.<id>; check.mjs link_guard) + the manifest web.routes (works only when both are present) Apps without a URL or web.routes get no link check on AI answers (URLs the AI made up or mistyped are delivered as they are; if web.routes exists, one warning on the first AI answer)

d.9 Personal bots (the person's own SNS)

  • MUST Each staff member configures only their own connections. Do not build screens or APIs that view, create or remove other people's connections (administrators included). The administrator's 「IM ボット接続」 (IM bot connections) does not show staff members' personal bots (excludeBotIds).
  • MUST Personal bots are created and changed through the self-service RPC of the business web app's BFF. A per-channel allow-list (no means of changing the working folder, model, preset, context enrichment or access policy is allowed); requests containing a botId only for the person's own bots (ask the business system every time); narrow the response bots[] to the person's own; create with createOnly: true (for an existing bot, bot-exists and nothing changes); register the new botId to the person with POST /bridge/v1/me/personal-bots, and on failure delete the bot to roll back. web-kit's self mode only hides components; it is not a safeguard.
  • MUST Only the BFF, right after a successful createOnly creation through the self-service RPC, attaches x-bff-secret to POST /bridge/v1/me/personal-bots. Do not relay browser requests with the secret (if you do, a person can register an organisation bot's botId as their own personal bot, and because of the lookup's owner rule every other staff member who talks to that bot becomes "unlinked". b.6).
  • MUST The business system's identity lookup (GET /bridge/v1/identity?…&botId=) returns linked for a botId that is a registered personal bot only when the link belongs to its owner (another staff member in the same workspace who talks to someone else's personal bot is not let through). A revoked personal bot lets no one through. server-kit has this rule (identityOf: botId is checked in GET /identity, POST /delegations and IM approval decisions alike; wechat is treated the same as weixin). The link code owner rule (personal_bot_owner_mismatch) and revocation on unlinking are also in server-kit. A business system that does not use server-kit implements the same rules itself (CareBilling: care-api's resolveIdentity).
  • SHOULD server-kit's personalBotPlatforms defaults to PERSONAL_BOT_PLATFORMS (slack, line, teams, telegram, discord, weixin, whatsapp, wecom, wecom-app, qq, dingtalk, feishu, matrix; email and iMessage are not included; the same as CareBilling). If some channel should not allow personal bots, narrow it (opt-out). Channels that need a public endpoint, such as LINE, Teams and WeCom self-built apps, are shown as 「準備中」 (coming soon) while the endpoint (DSH_PUBLIC_HOOK_PATHS) is missing.

d.10 Long-term memory (bridge-memory)

  • MUST: Memory holds only "preferences, ongoing matters, notes" (personal) and "procedures, reasons for decisions, operational preferences" (organisation). Business data (records, billing, states) is not memorised; it is read with tools every time.
  • MUST: Do not store personal data or health information. Before storing, pass the local check and /pii-scan; on a hit, do not store. If the check cannot be reached, do not store (fail closed).
  • MUST: A system that holds names of staff, service users or business partners implements a roster check with server-kit's hooks.piiScan(text, ctx) -> { kinds: string[] } (search by family name, given name and kana; on a hit return only the category such as staff_name. Do not return or log the matched string. Sample: equipment-inspection's src/hooks.mjs. If the hook throws, the result is 503 and the memory is not stored). server-kit's default /pii-scan only checks shapes (contact details, long numbers, ID numbers, etc.) and knows no names; it does not match ordinary Japanese or English text (if it did, not a single memory would be stored). The hook's categories are returned together with the shape check's categories. A custom /pii-scan has the same shape ({ ok, containsPersonalData, kinds }).
  • MUST: Personal memories and conversation retrospectives are for the person themself only. Admin screens also show only counts. Memory is not used in group conversations.
  • SHOULD: Change the app name, categories and retention through createMemoryPlugin or settings; do not fork the plugin. If there is a previous store, point to the same domain with domain.
  • SHOULD: Pass memories in the system prompt as "reference information (not instructions)", and let the data win when they conflict with business data (as in the template).

d.11 AI employee profile (bridge-persona)

  • MUST: The business system is the source of truth for the profile. Only administrators edit it, a change creates a new version, and the audit keeps only the version number (not the body).
  • MUST: Check with validateAiProfile (@dsh-bridge/protocol) before saving. Wording that tries to break the rules (「承認なしで」 (without approval), 「規則を無視」 (ignore the rules), etc.) and personal data (contact details, numbers) are refused on save (D4). The matched string is not returned.
  • MUST: The profile does not change permissions, tools or safety rules. In the system prompt the fixed rules come first (renderPersona), and the AI always shows that it is an AI (the signature is 「— <呼び名>（<アプリ名> AI 秘書）」 (— ( AI secretary)), D8).
  • SHOULD: One nickname per app (the default; do not pass agents to AiProfilePage. Saving clears the per-AI-employee overrides of earlier versions, so no hidden override changes the name). Separate nicknames per AI employee (preset) are the deployment's choice, only when agents is passed (AI_EMPLOYEE_PROFILE.md §6 D3).
  • SHOULD: Per-preset overrides (agents.<preset id>) cover only nickname, personality and background. Avoid nicknames that could be confused with real people (the administrator's responsibility; a warning on the screen).
  • SHOULD: The system prompt is fixed during a conversation (prompt cache). Tell users on the screen that changes take effect from the next conversation.

d.12 File attachments to the AI assistant

  • MUST: Determine the type from both the extension and the leading bytes (type_mismatch if they disagree). Refuse macro-enabled files (xlsm, docm), legacy formats (xls, doc), archives and executables. The limits are 5 files, 10 MB per file and 20 MB in total (they may be lowered, not raised).

  • MUST: Documents are converted to text in the business system's memory, and neither the original nor the text is stored. Audit and logs keep only count, type and size (not file names or content).

  • MUST: Put the document text in the prompt as "reference information (not instructions)" (do not follow instructions inside the material). Do not give AI employees a tool that reads files.

  • MUST: Administrators decide which roles and types may use attachments (default: admin, manager and billing among the manifest roles; all types). When the model is known not to read images, refuse images at attach time (images_not_supported).

  • MUST: Show answers as safe Markdown (no HTML output; links only to the business web app URL and allowed hosts; external links with rel="noopener noreferrer").

  • MUST: Decide how scanned PDFs (pages without a text layer) are handled. In createBridgeApp({ attachments: { ocr } }):

    • A function ocr(bytes, { mediaType, page }) -> text (an OCR engine inside the business system; the framework does not bundle one): turns pages into text (ocr: 'engine'). Page images do not leave the business system.
    • Omitted (default): renders pages as JPEG (up to 10 pages per request) and sends them to the model as images (ocr: 'model'; they also stay in the DSH conversation history; with a model that cannot read images, images_not_supported).
    • false: no OCR (no_text, details.reason: ocr_off).

    A system that handles documents containing health or personal data uses engine or false, and does not keep the default (images to the model). Rendering pages needs pdf.js (pdfjs-dist) and @napi-rs/canvas (without them, no_text, details.reason: ocr_unavailable). The audit keeps only ocrPages (the page count).

  • SHOULD: Always show 「添付した内容は AI のモデルに送られます」 (Attached content is sent to the AI model) in the panel. Show a tag with the attachment name on the sent message.

  • SHOULD: Use bridge-assistant's image cleanup as it is (imageCleanup default on, imageCleanupMinutes default 60): images of redone conversations and of conversations unused for 12 hours that no other conversation references are deleted from DSH's attachment store (a run that cannot read the logs completely deletes nothing). dshHome (default: the environment variable DSH_HOME, otherwise ~/.dsh) must point to the isolated home that DSH runs in (d.7).

Business document intake (the AI reads scanned PDFs and images, docs/DOCUMENT_READS.md)

  • If you have a screen that imports images or PDFs without a text layer, implement server-kit's hooks.documentReads = { claim({ limit }, ctx), answer(readId, body, ctx) } to enable GET /bridge/v1/document-reads / POST /bridge/v1/document-reads/{readId}/result (an optional feature, service token), and provide the page images (JPEG / PNG, up to 10 pages; for PDFs, the ocrPages of createPdfTextExtractor). DSH's bridge-reader has a model that can read images transcribe each page once and returns the text (no conversation is created).
  • MUST: Every field built from the returned text is put in a state that needs human confirmation (values the AI read are never finalised automatically). Business decisions (which service user, which values to import) belong to the business system and people.
  • MUST: Page images are sent to the model provider. Provide a setting to stop this and explain it on the screen. Logs and audit keep only counts, IDs and error codes (no images or read text).
  • Do not put person names in hint (the form name). A claim may be handed out again after 10 minutes (an answer to an old claim gets 409 read_not_claimed).

d.13 External connectors (connections, operations, rules)

  • MUST: Secrets (API keys, passwords, client secrets) are held only by the business system. An administrator sends them once from the business web app, and server-kit seals and stores them (the screen shows only the last 4 characters). The sealing key (connectors.secretKey) is passed from an environment variable. Do not write it in the DSH profile, manifest, prompts, logs or repository.
  • MUST: The AI can execute only reads (the delegated staff member's role ∈ operation.roles). A write goes connector_write proposal → approval by an authorised person → executed by the business system. A rule's auto covers only reads and idempotent writes that an administrator allowed with a written reason.
  • MUST: Connections are https and allowed hosts only (localhost for development via allowLocalhost, never in production). Only the fields in the operation input's JSON Schema are sent, and only the responseFields allow-list is returned to the AI. Operations with a high personal-data category are used in rules only when an administrator explicitly sets allowPii.
  • MUST: Execution records, audit and IM notices contain only IDs, counts and states (input and response bodies are not output to IM or logs).
  • SHOULD: Start with one or two reads. Tell operators where the emergency stop (/admin/connector-settings) and the per-connection and per-rule stops are.

e. Testing policy

Layer With what What it verifies
Unit node --test in each package (pnpm test) Component contracts. Business APIs are mocked with node:http; data is fictitious
Conformance packages/protocol/conformance (52 checks) That the business system keeps the protocol's invariants. A mutation test (test/conformance-mutants.test.mjs) also confirms that breaking an invariant makes the check fail
manifest bridge-validate manifest / pnpm validate Schema, cross-references, keys that look like PII
e2e (mock) pnpm run e2e (packages/testing/e2e/run.mjs) Runs the real DSH + vendor fork + plugins + gateway end to end with a mock LLM / LINE (a linking → b question → c notification → d approval → e automatic task → f isolation; 15 / 15 steps, about 70 seconds; a.3). Currently equipment-inspection only (for a new system, write your own scenario with the components of @dsh-bridge/testing, or judge by items 2 and 3 of the Definition of Done)
Full flow (planned) full-flow runner Starts the business system (TEST DB), DSH and a mock IM together, and verifies in one scenario everything from an operation in the business web app to delivery in the IM. Per-business scenarios live in each business system's repository
Real devices Manual Checks in a real IM (section g, roadmap)
  • e2e rules: test values only (generated every run), loopback only, an isolated DSH home, and the ports of the demo environment and production are rejected with assertPortsUsable(ports, { forbidden }). sanitizedEnv drops real API keys, tokens, DB URLs and any existing DSH_* BRIDGE_* CARE_*.
  • Windows notes
    • Run node --test with --test-isolation=none (as in each package's script).
    • Check out vendor/dsh-im with LF (with core.autocrlf=true, CRs get into string constants and change the build output and the i18n tests).
    • Windows fails rename with EPERM on a file that another handle has open: the fork retries briefly (renameReplacing).
    • Some upstream tests of dsh-im skip / fail for Windows-specific reasons (FORK.md). In environments where esbuild cannot write to %TEMP%, point TEMP / TMP to another directory.
    • Do not start child processes by running a .cmd through a shell (stopping the shell leaves the actual process running). Use killTree.
    • Under heavy load (several test runs at once), timing-dependent tests can fail. Re-run them on their own.

f. Versioning (protocol / manifest)

Target How the version is expressed Rules
Protocol Path /bridge/v1, header bridge-protocol: 1, bridge: 1 in the manifest, OpenAPI info.version (1.0.0) Within v1, additions only (optional fields, new operations, new error codes). Changing meaning, removing fields or adding required ones means v2 (/bridge/v2). When the protocol changes, change the conformance suite at the same time
Error codes lower snake case in x-error-codes Stable identifiers. Do not embed field names (required + details.field). The human-readable message may change
manifest version (SemVer or a date); the etag comes from the content When the content changes, the etag changes and DSH re-fetches with If-None-Match (manifestRefreshSeconds, default 600 seconds). An invalid or unreachable manifest does not replace the last valid one
Event types <aggregate>.<fact> A type no longer emitted is not removed but marked deprecated: true (so past events stay valid). Removing a payload key is a change in the type's meaning
playbook Redeployed only when the manifest version changes Only the fields the template owns (name, instruction, trigger, approval, source, applicationId, audience, sessionPreset) are overwritten; operational fields (enabled, delivery, guard, run state) are kept. A playbook removed from the manifest is disabled (not deleted)
Packages @dsh-bridge/* 0.1.0 (private); the fork is <upstream>-care.N SemVer once published. The licence is undecided (LICENSE)

dsh-core also accepts responses without the bridge-protocol header (compatibility with older systems). If the value is not 1, it raises BridgeProtocolError.

g. FAQ and troubleshooting

A notification stays "pending" and is not delivered

  1. It is within the wait of a digest send (short-window or periodic) (realtimeSettleSeconds 15 seconds / realtimeDigestSeconds 2 minutes / digestMinutes). Use ctx.bridgeNotify.flushNow() or, for verification, digestMinutes: 0.
  2. The recipient's quiet hours (held until they end). Only kinds with notify.quiet: exempt are not held.
  3. Delivery priority: it is sent to the highest-priority linked platform. If that platform's bot is not connected (bot_offline), retries continue. See the reason (errorCode) in the reports of status().
  4. Bot: messages are sent only from that app's bot. Check bots in the registry and the bot used for linking.

No notification arrives (and no error either)

  • recipientsFor returned { stale } (the situation changed: already inspected, out of use, etc.) → not sending is correct. Old events are dropped by design.
  • The person's notification setting is off (kinds with notify.default: off in the manifest are off by default), or it was already notified (sent is terminal).
  • While the notification receiver (plugin-notify) has just started and is not yet registered, sends are treated as failures and retried (notifyGraceSeconds 120 seconds).

A notification reaches only some people (someone who should get it does not)

  • The business system's gate dropped them (the person cannot see the target in the business web app, or does not hold a role in the rule). Look at the reason code left in the business system's audit log (notification.recipient_denied in CareBilling). The right fix is to correct the affiliation / assignment scope; do not remove the gate.
  • Automatic task reports: no recipient was determined (cron-triggered, or a kind that does not notify). With audienceFallback: none nothing is sent (status().audienceSuppressed).

The AI does not answer in a group conversation

  • This is the correct behaviour (groupChat: deny). It returns only a fixed notice. Ask business questions in a 1:1 conversation.

The scheduled report became fixed wording (「業務 Web のダッシュボードで確認」 (Check the dashboard in the business web app))

  • The send guard found amounts, personal names, contact details, external URLs, long text or health-related words in the body (aiReportGuard: screen). The reason code appears in the DSH log. If business terms match the health-related word list, review the list (d.8).
  • The trigger guard stopped it: the person is disabled, not linked, in a different conversation, or in a role that is not allowed. Scheduled reports for that conversation stop, so the person sends 「定時報告 オン」 (Scheduled report on) again.

The AI says it "cannot read business data"

  • Not linked (linked: false). Issue a link code in the business web app and send it to that app's bot.
  • Automatic tasks / scheduled reports: delegation is denied by default (unattendedPolicy: deny). Configure the delegate in b.7. Scheduled reports run only when the person has turned on 「定時報告 オン」 in that conversation.
  • The conversation's app differs from the tool's app (another app is selected on a shared bot). Check with #いま (now) and switch with #<アプリ名> (#<app name>).
  • The tool's roles do not include the staff member's role (delegation = AI allow list ∩ role). Check tools[].roles in the manifest.

An automatic task (playbook) does not run

  • Deployed playbooks stay disabled: run install.mjs --enable-auto-tasks pb_<application-id>_<playbook> with the id given explicitly (without an id nothing is enabled). Do this after DSH has started once and plugin-events has deployed them.
  • The playbook's agent preset is not in the product profile → the dedicated conversation cannot be opened (no_session in the task's lastError).
  • There is no delegate (unattendedPolicy: deny), or the delegate staff member's role cannot use the playbook's tools.
  • The playbook is <class>=each but consent was not given with --auto-task-delegate <class>=each (install.mjs warns), or the business system does not issue a delegation for that event (404 / 422 / 409 / 403: no such event, a kind that does not get delegation, stale, or the person is not a subject). A default staff member is not substituted.
  • It runs only once per event (dedupe). To try again, raise a new event.

delegation_not_permitted / role_not_permitted A write API was called under delegation (delegation allows read and proposal only), or the proposal kind is one the role cannot handle. This is the correct behaviour.

Linking fails 404 / 410 (invalid / expired), 409 (already linked), 429 (too many attempts; wait 10 minutes). Group conversations are not accepted. Linking is not possible via email. With a personal bot, only the person who registered that bot can link (someone else's code is rejected with personal_bot_owner_mismatch).

Creating a personal bot is refused with bot-exists A bot with the same credentials (same token, same account) already exists (the organisation bot, or someone else's personal bot). createOnly refuses without changing anything. Create a different bot (a different token).

DSH starts slowly / the first request fails On first run, install the profile's bundle (dsh plugin --profile <name> install). The manifest is fetched from manifestUrl at startup; if unreachable, manifestFile is used. The gateway re-acquires the launch token on a DSH 401 (restart, expiry) and resends GET / HEAD / upgrade only once. In e2e, startDsh waits for the launch token line. If dsh --version differs from the profile's dshBridge.expectedDsh, install.mjs warns.

The same notification / report arrived twice The idempotency key is "recorded after success", so if the process dies right after the IM side accepted the message, exactly one message may be resent (a known limitation of dsh-im). If it happens in any other case, check how the idempotency key is built (whether retries use the same key).

On a shared bot, a reply went to a different app Reply by quoting, or reply within 10 minutes of the notification, and it goes back to the notification's app. Otherwise it goes to the "current app". Check with #一覧 (list).

The nickname does not appear in the signature / panel, or the way of speaking does not change after editing the profile

  • The business system has no GET /bridge/v1/ai-profile (404), or paths.aiProfile in the registry is empty: it runs without a profile (signature 「— <アプリ名> AI 秘書」 (— AI secretary)).
  • DSH re-fetches only at startup and every aiProfileRefreshSeconds (default 60 seconds). If the fetch fails or a value fails validation, the previous value is kept (app.aiProfileInfo().lastError).
  • The system prompt section is fixed per conversation: changes apply from the next conversation (/new). The signature and panel heading change from the next successful fetch.

The AI does not save "remember this"

  • It contains personal data (personal names with honorifics, contact details, long numbers, health-related words), the business system's /pii-scan returned a category (for example the roster hook hooks.piiScan found a name), or /pii-scan is unreachable (fail closed). It is also not used in group conversations or unlinked conversations (d.10). If even ordinary sentences are not saved, check whether the business system's /pii-scan flags the text itself (cjk_text / free_text) (the server-kit default does not).

Links in AI answers are not checked (one link guard warning in the DSH log)

  • The app's business web app URL is missing: linkGuard.webUrl for the default app, linkGuard.webUrls.<application-id> for other apps (b.8).

Logs and secrets The launch token is masked in logs (redactToken). Do not paste tokens or passwords into issues or logs.

h. Reference implementation: CareBilling

CareBilling (care-billing, repository care-ai-native) is the first adopter of the framework, and had its own versions of the same components before the framework existed. examples/care-billing contains the following (no business code):

  • manifest: system id care-billing, namespace care, 5 roles (admin, manager, billing, staff, care_manager), 71 events (1 deprecated, 65 that notify), 92 templates, 46 recipient rules, 27 tools (including the manual search care_help_search), 5 playbooks, report daily_status, help, 131 web.routes (version 2026-10-29; counts re-taken from the manifest on 2026-10-30).
  • The mapping table of care-api routes ↔ v1 (care-api-v1-aliases.md / .json): care-api exposes v1 as aliases on its existing /api/ai/* and other routes (b.2').
  • registry/bridge-apps.yaml: registry entries (Slack, LINE, WeCom, a shared personal WeChat) and extension modules.
  • extensions/README.md: the table of template intents (92), the care_* tools (29 = 27 in the manifest + 2 plugin-only), playbooks and delegation classes, presets.
  • The mapping table "framework component → where CareBilling implements it" (which CareBilling file holds each server-kit hook, each DSH plugin and each web-kit screen).

When in doubt, compare both equipment-inspection (the minimal implementation on top of server-kit) and CareBilling (an implementation that puts aliases on the existing API of a large system). CareBilling is also a sample for how recipients are decided (decideRecipients in services/care-api/src/repo/notifications.mjs, with the gate in repo/notify-scope.mjs), the RPC for the person themself (apps/care-web/me-im-rpc.mjs), per-event delegation (repo/identity.mjs) and outbound settings (dsh/runtime-profile/cordis.patch.yml). The design rationale is in care-ai-native's docs/design/NOTIFY_RECIPIENTS.md, IM_PERSONAL_BOTS.md and ROLE_MODEL.md (U10).

Added on 2026-10-29 (location in CareBilling):

  • Manual and how-to questions over SNS: docs/manual (164 sections), the index and CI tools/manual-index.mjs and services/care-api/test/help-manual.test.mjs, search GET /api/help/search (v1 alias), tool care_help_search (plugins/care-tools/src/help.js), help screen apps/care-web/src/pages/Help.tsx. Design: docs/design/SNS_HELP_QA.md.
  • Long-term memory: plugins/care-memory (only createMemoryPlugin configuration: the former tool names care_memory_*, storage care_memory, and omitting scope means facility memory), check POST /api/ai/pii-scan.
  • AI employee profile: services/care-api/sql/096_ai_profile.sql (ai_profile_version), src/routes/ai-profile.mjs (GET /api/ai/ai-profile and the admin /api/ai-profile, v1 aliases), screen 「管理 › AI 社員の設定」 (Admin › AI employee settings) /settings/ai-profile (apps/care-web/src/pages/settings/AiProfile.tsx, web-kit AiProfilePage), signature 「— さくら（ケアビリング AI 秘書）」 (— Sakura (CareBilling AI secretary)) (care-notify). Design: docs/design/AI_PROFILE_CARE.md.
